results.summary_before: This design converts between ASCII serial data and Baudot serial data using UARTs and two conversion ROMs. It accepts an ASCII clock at eight times the desired baud rate and a Baudot clock at one hundred times the desired baud rate, with a Baudot input that should be held high when idle. The outputs drive a seven-segment display to show the converted data. External hardware includes a USB-serial adapter for ASCII and a 60 mA current loop interface for Baudot, which requires a hefty driver.

The outputs are mapped to seven-segment display segment pins. External hardware includes a USB-serial adapter for ASCII and a 60 mA current loop interface for Baudot, which requires a hefty driver.

The operation is selected by two arithOp input bits, and a state machine requires the enable signal to be released before another operation can be triggered. The eight-bit result is shown on the LED outputs, and the design is tested by toggling switches on the demo board. It is a simple arithmetic demonstration with no external hardware beyond the board switches and LEDs.

results.summary_before: This project implements three pulse-density modulator architectures: PWM, DDPM, and Sigma-Delta, for digital-to-analog conversion. It includes both a 6-bit DC input section and an 8-bit sine wave section to evaluate spectral performance. The outputs are intended to be low-pass filtered to recover the analog signal, and the design is implemented using myHDL and Python. It serves as a comparison of different PDM techniques for DAC applications.

results.summary_before: This project plays the song 'Bad Apple' through a piezo speaker connected across two output pins using differential PWM modulation. It converts an RTTL ringtone into Verilog and plays it back when a 12 kHz clock is provided and a reset pulse is applied. The design requires an external piezo speaker connected between io_out[0] and io_out[1]. It is notable for being a simple music player based on a previous Tiny Tapeout project.
